newsitem.title: USA: US stocks seen flat to lower at open, eyes on NAPM.
newsitem.headline: US stocks seen flat to lower at open, eyes on NAPM.

text.p: Wall Street stocks are expected to open flat to lower ahead of the release of September's National Association of Purchasing Managament (NAPM) index.
The NAPM index, always closely watched by markets, will draw even more attention Tuesday because of a surprisingly sharp jump in the price component of the regional Chicago index, released yesterday.
"If today's NAPM prices paid component is like yesterday's in the Chicago index, that would be a major jump," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments.
The Chicago Managers report showed an increase in the prices paid index to 59.3, its highest level in more than a year, from August's 51.8.
"A major jump like that could push the long bond back over seven percent," Cardillo said, "and every time we get to seven percent the (stock) market has had difficulty."
The NAPM report is due at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT. At 0830 EDT/1230 GMT, the August index of leading economic indicators will be released.
Beyond the NAPM-related caution, markets will be wary after seeing Monday's rally fell apart in the last moments.
"We faded yesterday and it seems the high-techs were a little tired at the end," said Larry Wachtel, market analyst at Prudential Securities. "It looks like we'll get more of that at the open."
Analysts also noted that the Dow industrials have struggled in repeated attempts to close over the 5900 level.
A tame reading in the NAPM prices component could offer some support in that rally, but analysts noted that the Chicago prices number has tended to correspond closely to the national figure.
In Tokyo, profit-taking pulled stocks lower, ending five straight sessions of gains. The Nikkei-225 index fell 93 points to 21,463.
In London, U.S. stocks met with mild selling pressure, with automobile shares leading the decliners. The FTSE-100 index climbed 25.7 points to 3979.4.
The dollar drifted lower in Tokyo but held above the 111 yen level. The greenback firmed in Europe, hitting resistance at just below 1.53 German marks.
U.S. Treasuries were slightly lower. The benchmark 30-year bond dipped 4/32 to yield 6.93 percent.
The S&P 500 index future edged up 0.5 to 691.9.

The New York Times Marketplace Column writes that the third quarter was a generally good one for stocks, despite the July correction. The column states the quarter's strongest performer was Federal Agricultural Mortgage Corp (FARMER MAC), which leaped 292 percent.

The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street column reports some analysts are expressing concern that Banc One Corp may become overly aggressive in acquisition efforts after its bid for Boatmens Bancshares failed.
